h1: Zinsco Panel Replacement in Broward County
intro: Most people who call us about a Zinsco panel did not go looking for the problem. It found them. An insurance company flagged it at renewal, or a 4-point inspection named the brand and would not pass the home. If that is you, here is the plain truth, stated once. Zinsco panels are an obsolete brand, and their breakers can fail to trip the way a breaker is supposed to when there is a fault. That is why carriers increasingly will not cover a home that has one. Replacing Zinsco and Federal Pacific panels is the single most common upgrade we perform, so this is familiar ground for us. We come out, we look at your service in person, and we replace the panel with modern, insurable equipment. No drama, just done.

definition.heading: What a Zinsco panel is
definition.body: Zinsco is a brand of electrical panel installed in many homes built decades ago, and it is no longer considered safe by today's standards. The concern is documented and specific. The breakers inside a Zinsco panel can fail to trip under a fault, which means the one part that is supposed to cut power in a dangerous moment may not do it. The bus bar the breakers connect to can also degrade over time. Because the equipment is obsolete, parts are hard to source and a real repair is usually not practical. That is why the honest answer is almost always replacement rather than patching. Insurance carriers in South Florida know the brand by name, which is why so many homeowners learn they have a Zinsco panel from a renewal notice or a 4-point inspection rather than from any obvious symptom.

symptoms.title: The brand name Zinsco is on the panel
symptoms.body: The clearest sign is the label itself. If the panel or the breakers read Zinsco, or the similar name Sylvania used on related equipment, that alone is reason for a licensed look. The brand, not a symptom, is what carriers and inspectors react to.

symptoms.title: Your insurer or 4-point flagged it
symptoms.body: A renewal notice or a 4-point inspection named the panel and will not pass the home. This is how most people find out. The carrier is reacting to the brand's documented history, and they will hold the policy until it is replaced.

symptoms.title: Breakers that do not trip or hold
symptoms.body: A breaker that will not reset, or one that clearly should have tripped and did not, is exactly the failure mode this brand is known for. That is the safety concern in plain terms, and it deserves attention rather than another reset.

symptoms.title: Warmth, buzzing, or a burning smell
symptoms.body: The panel feels warm, hums, or gives off a burning smell. Electricity is something we do not see, we only feel the effect. On an aging Zinsco panel those effects are worth taking seriously and looking at soon.

symptoms.title: Discoloration or scorch at the breakers
symptoms.body: You see browning, melting, or scorch marks where the breakers meet the bus. That is heat and degradation at the exact connection point this brand struggles with. It is a clear sign the equipment has reached the end of its service life.

symptoms.title: Colored breaker handles in an old panel
symptoms.body: Many Zinsco panels carry breakers with distinctive colored handles inside older equipment. If that looks familiar, have it identified by a licensed electrician. Knowing for certain is the first calm step toward getting the home insurable again.

localSections.heading: Why Zinsco panels are so common in South Florida
localSections.body: Zinsco panels went into a great many homes during a long stretch of building in the middle of the last century, and Broward County did a lot of growing in exactly that window. That timing is why the brand turns up so often when we open panels from West Palm Beach down to North Miami. A home can pass from owner to owner for decades with the same Zinsco panel quietly sitting in the garage or on an exterior wall, never touched because it seemed to work fine. Working fine and being safe are not the same thing with this brand, which is the whole issue. None of this makes your home unusual. It makes it typical of its era. When we tell a homeowner they have a Zinsco panel, we are almost never surprised to find it, and neither should you be. It is simply part of owning a South Florida home built in a certain decade, and it has a clean, well-understood fix.

localSections.heading: Heat and salt air on aging equipment
localSections.body: A Zinsco panel that has spent decades in the South Florida climate has not had an easy life. Constant heat keeps the internal components warm. Humidity works its way into the enclosure. Homes closer to the coast deal with salt air that slowly corrodes the bus bar and the terminations, and the bus is exactly the part of this brand that is known to degrade. A connection that has loosened or corroded runs hotter than it should, and on equipment already prone to trouble, that heat accelerates the wear. This is why an aging Zinsco panel down here can be in worse shape inside than it looks from the outside. When we assess one, the condition of the bus and the breaker contacts tells us a lot. We factor the real environment into the forecast, so the replacement we quote is built to hold up in the heat and humidity it has to live in.

localSections.heading: Permitting and code reality in Broward
localSections.body: Replacing a Zinsco panel in Broward County is permitted work, and that is a good thing for you. The permit puts a licensed contractor and a county inspector between you and a mistake, and it creates the documentation your insurance carrier will want to see. Electrical code moves on a multi-year cycle, so the new panel we install is built to the current standard, not the one from when the Zinsco panel first went in. We pull the permit, schedule the inspection, and we meet the inspector on site in person. That matters when the whole reason for the job is to satisfy a carrier. The team that priced your replacement and knows every detail of it is standing there when Broward County signs off, so the paperwork that protects your policy is handled correctly and completely, with nothing left hanging.

localSections.heading: How carriers treat the Zinsco name
localSections.body: South Florida insurance carriers know the Zinsco name, and many of them react to it directly. A 4-point inspection that identifies the brand can be enough for a carrier to decline a new policy or drop an existing one at renewal, even on a home that has never had an electrical problem you noticed. This is honest, verifiable reality, and it is why a homeowner who felt fine about the panel suddenly has a deadline. We describe it plainly and without alarm because there is no need to dramatize it. The path forward is clear and we have walked it many times. Replace the obsolete panel with modern, code-compliant equipment, pass the county inspection, and the specific objection tied to the Zinsco name is gone. Then your policy can proceed on the strength of a service the carrier has no reason to question.

guide.title: The complete guide to Zinsco panel replacement in South Florida

sections.heading: What a Zinsco panel is and why it matters
sections.body: Zinsco is a brand of electrical panel that was installed widely in homes built decades ago, including a great many across Broward County. Your panel is the point where power from the utility is divided into the circuits that run your home, and the breakers inside it are the safety devices that are supposed to cut power the instant something goes wrong. The concern with Zinsco is specific and documented, and we will state it once, plainly. The breakers in a Zinsco panel can fail to trip under a fault, and the bus bar they connect to can degrade over time. In other words, the one part of your electrical system whose entire job is to protect you in a dangerous moment may not do that job. That is the whole issue, and it is enough. We do not need to dress it up or scare you with it. It simply means this equipment has reached the end of its trustworthy life and the honest answer is to replace it.

sections.heading: Why replacement, not repair, is the honest answer
sections.body: People sometimes ask whether a Zinsco panel can just be repaired, and it is a fair question. The honest answer is almost always no, and here is why. The brand is obsolete, so genuine parts are difficult to source and often are not truly new. More important, the concern is not one broken piece you can swap out. It is the design of the breakers and the condition of the bus itself, which are the core of the panel. Patching one breaker does not address the reason carriers and inspectors react to the whole unit. Spending money to keep an obsolete panel alive is money that would be better put toward a modern one that solves the problem for good and satisfies your insurance company at the same time. We would rather tell you that straight than sell you a repair that leaves the real issue in place. Price it once, price it right, and be done with it. That is the approach that actually serves you.

sections.heading: When replacement becomes urgent
sections.body: For many owners a Zinsco panel sits quietly for years and the push to replace it comes from outside the home. The most common trigger in South Florida is insurance. A 4-point inspection identifies the brand, and your carrier tells you the policy will not renew until the panel is replaced. That turns a someday project into a dated one, often with a renewal deadline attached. The second trigger is a symptom we can see. When we find scorching at the bus, breakers that do not trip or hold, or heat damage during an assessment, replacement moves from a good idea to the clear recommendation. The third is simply peace of mind. Some owners, once they understand what the brand is, decide they do not want to keep sleeping above equipment that may not protect them. Any of those reasons is a good one. We will tell you honestly which situation you are in, and we will not manufacture urgency that is not there. If the panel is stable and the only pressure is a carrier deadline, we will help you understand the timeline honestly, so you can plan the work around your budget and your renewal rather than feeling rushed into it. A real deadline deserves a straight answer, not a scare tactic.

sections.heading: What the day of the work looks like
sections.body: Replacing a Zinsco panel is focused, familiar work for our crew, because it is the single most common upgrade we perform. It is an in and out type of situation. That is what we do. We coordinate with the utility so the power feeding the property can be interrupted safely for the work window. Then our in-house crew removes the Zinsco panel, installs modern equipment in its place, and reconnects every circuit, labeling as we go so you end up with a panel you can actually read. We check and correct the grounding and the connections, because a new panel is only as good as what feeds it. You will be without power for part of the day, and we tell you honestly ahead of time so you can plan around it. Because the same crew does this constantly, there is a rhythm to it and the property is left clean. When the work is done we schedule the county inspection so your carrier gets the documentation it needs. Before the day, there is little you need to do beyond clearing some room around the panel and planning for the hours without power. If someone in the home works remotely or depends on medical equipment, tell us when we schedule, and we will build the window around that. We would rather plan around your life than ask you to plan around ours. Small courtesies like that are part of giving a customer more than what they pay for.

sections.heading: An honest conversation about cost
sections.body: A Zinsco panel replacement is quoted per property after an on-site assessment, and there is a good reason we do not post a flat number. What the job takes depends on the condition of the existing service, the grounding, the size the property needs, and what we uncover when we open things up. Two homes with the same Zinsco panel can carry very different jobs behind the cover. Our service call is $240, which covers roughly two hours including travel, arrival, and diagnosis, and if the problem can be handled on the spot there is no separate return charge. For the replacement itself, we forecast what the job actually takes and give you one price before we begin, and that price does not change mid-job. We do not add fees partway through. Price it once, price it right. If a low bid from someone else looks tempting, ask what it does not include. Losing an honestly priced job is fine with us. Winning one and padding it later is something we do not do.

sections.heading: How to choose the right contractor for this work
sections.body: Because a panel sits at the center of your home's safety and the reason for this job is often your insurance, the contractor you choose matters as much as the equipment. Start with licensing. Ghost Crown Electric is a Florida Certified Electrical Contractor with statewide authority and a Broward County Master Electrician, with 286 permitted projects on public record. Ask whether the contractor can pull the permit in their own name and who attends the inspection, because when the team that priced the job meets the inspector, the documentation your carrier needs gets handled right. Ask who does the work. An in-house crew that replaces these panels constantly is not the same as a rotating set of subcontractors seeing one for the first time. And be wary of anyone who sells by running down every other company or by inventing urgency. We do not do that. We state the concern with Zinsco once, we let our license and our record speak, and we give a customer more than what they pay for. A good contractor should also be willing to explain the Zinsco concern in plain language, without either brushing it off or leaning on fear to close the sale. If someone cannot tell you calmly why the brand is a problem and what replacing it actually solves, that is worth noticing. We are happy to walk you through exactly what we see in your panel and why our recommendation is what it is, and then to let you make the call in your own time.

sections.heading: After the replacement: what changes
sections.body: Once the Zinsco panel is gone and modern equipment is in its place, a few real things change for you. The insurance objection tied to the brand is removed, so your policy can proceed on a service the carrier has no reason to question, and the 4-point item that failed now passes. The breakers protecting your home will trip when they are supposed to, which is the entire point of having them. Proper grounding and solid connections mean the heart of your electrical system runs cool and quiet. Grounding here is not a gimmick and we do not frame it as anything it is not. It protects your family, your home, and your investment as a whole, and it is part of doing the job right. Beyond all of that, you get to stop thinking about the panel, which is worth something on its own. We show up when we say we will, we replace the equipment properly, and then it simply works, quietly, in the background, the way it should have all along. If your policy paperwork needs the inspection record or the permit details, we make sure you have exactly what your carrier asks for, so the last mile of getting insured again is as smooth as the work itself. We do not consider the job done until you are covered and comfortable.
